title: Kepler's third law: T² = a³
caption: With a in AU and T in years, T = a^{3/2} for every planet. Earth (1 AU) has T = 1 year; Jupiter at 5.2 AU has T = 5.2^{3/2} = 11.86 years. Doubling the orbit radius multiplies the period by 2^{3/2} ≈ 2.8, not 2.
alt: Graph of orbital period in years against semi-major axis in astronomical units: a curve T equals a to the power 3 over 2, through Earth at (1, 1) and Jupiter at (5.2, 11.9).
description: The horizontal axis is the semi-major axis a in AU; the vertical axis is the period T in years.
The curve is T = a^{3/2}, which is T² = a³ in these units.
Earth sits at (1, 1) by definition of the AU and the year.
Jupiter: a = 5.2 AU gives T = 11.86 years.
